title: Rayleigh Bound States in the Continuum
authors: Ilya Karavaev, Mingzhao Song, Andrey Bogdanov
abstract: We predict a class of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in non-subwavelength periodic metasurfaces -- Rayleigh BICs -- that emerge precisely at Rayleigh anomalies, where diffraction channels open. In contrast to conventional symmetry-protected and accidental BICs, which are typically engineered in the subwavelength regime with only a few radiation channels, Rayleigh BICs remain nonradiating far beyond this limit, even when multiple diffraction channels are open. Their formation originates from the interplay between collective lattice resonances, Rayleigh anomalies, and anapole states of the constituent metaatoms. We show that Rayleigh BICs are characterized by an unusual cubic scaling of the quality factor in reciprocal space, ($Q \propto 1/k^3$), an asymptotic behavior that is not characteristic of either symmetry-protected or accidental BICs. Our results establish a constructive route for engineering nonradiating states in metasurfaces beyond the subwavelength regime.
summary: The paper introduces Rayleigh BICs, a new mechanism for creating nonradiating states in periodic metasurfaces operating beyond the subwavelength limit. These states arise from the coupling of lattice resonances with anapole frequencies exactly at diffraction anomalies. The key finding is that these BICs possess a unique cubic scaling of their quality factor, offering a robust design route for optical engineering.
main_problem: The research aims to predict and engineer a novel class of Bound States in the Continuum (BICs) that remain nonradiating even when multiple diffraction channels are open, specifically operating beyond the subwavelength regime.
main_result: A distinct class of Rayleigh BICs is predicted to emerge at the intersection of collective lattice resonances and Rayleigh anomalies. These states exhibit a unique cubic scaling of the quality factor ($Q \propto 1/k^3$), confirming their robustness beyond conventional BIC mechanisms.
method: The analysis employs multiple-scattering theory within the dipole approximation, focusing on the analytic structure of the reflection coefficient to identify conditions for nonradiating poles.
model_or_system: The study models non-subwavelength periodic metasurfaces using a lattice of lossless point electric dipoles arranged on a square lattice. The physics involves coupling between lattice resonances, anapole states, and the opening of diffraction channels at Rayleigh anomalies.
key_observables: Reflectance ($R$), Quality factor ($Q$ factor), and the frequency/momentum dependence of the BIC location.
important_parameters: The periodicity ($a$) relative to the wavelength, the incidence angle ($	heta$), and the degree of coupling between lattice resonances and anapole frequencies.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dipole approximation initially, though extensions consider higher-order multipoles. The BIC condition requires simultaneous vanishing of both numerator and denominator of the reflection coefficient.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate single dipole scattering efficiency (showing Mie/anapole resonances), the reflectance spectrum showing transparency at anapole frequencies, and detailed plots pinpointing the Rayleigh BIC location where $Q$ diverges.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining BICs in metasurfaces, then identifying the specific mechanism—the interplay between lattice resonance crossing the anapole frequency precisely at a Rayleigh anomaly. It contrasts this with conventional BICs and quantifies its unique $Q$-factor scaling.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical framework for engineering high-quality optical cavities in structured materials, which is highly relevant to quantum optics applications like low-loss waveguides or enhanced sensing platforms.
